title: Artificial intelligence versus physician decision-making in acute heart failure: a comparative evaluation of four contemporary AI systems
summary: diagnostic performance and recommendation agreement varied by system/task.
ai_technology: four AI systems assessed standardized acute-heart-failure cases and outputs were compared with physician decisions across diagnosis, treatment, timing and prognosis.
organization: 3rd Department of Cardiology, ‘Sotiria’ Chest Diseases Hospital, Medical School, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, Mesogeion 152, Athens 11527, Greece; 3rd Cardiology Department, ‘Sotiria’ General Hospital of Chest Diseases of Athens, Athina Ioanni Martinou Endowed Chair, Medical School, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, Athens, Greece; School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, National Technical University of Athens, Athens, Greece

evidence.tested: diagnostic performance and recommendation agreement varied by system/task. Retrospective single-centre case comparison; task-specific clinical decision evaluation, no patient outcome or deployment effect.
evidence.unknown: not patient benefit or deployment outcomes.
evidence.ai_role: four AI systems assessed standardized acute-heart-failure cases and outputs were compared with physician decisions across diagnosis, treatment, timing and prognosis.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
